newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian government retains narrow poll lead.
newsitem.headline: Australian government retains narrow poll lead.

text.p: The Australian government had a four percentage point lead over the Labor Opposition as last week's federal 1997/98 budget failed to significantly boost government support, according to a newspaper opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The Australian's Newspoll found primary support for the Liberal-National coalition rose one point to 41 percent, while support for Labor fell two points to 37 percent.
As preferred prime minister, John Howard's rating remained steady at 45 percent, while Labor Leader Kim Beazley's rating rose five points to 27 percent.
But 28 percent of those surveyed remained uncommitted.
The latest result compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election that saw Howard sweep into power, ending 13 years of Labor rule.
When asked how good or bad the budget would be for the Australian economy, 33 percent of adults surveyed said it was good and 30 percent said it was bad.
The poll found that only two percent believed the budget was extremely good while 10 percent believed it was extremely bad.
The poll surveyed 1,151 voters around the country by telephone over the last weekend.
